candidate.title: Moleculo
candidate.scope: The supplied Illumina Moleculo product-preparation schematic: approximately 10 kb sheared genomic DNA is end repaired and adapter ligated, used to generate amplified clonal pools, processed in three parallel illustrated branches by tagmentation and index addition, and pooled/purified into prepared short DNA fragments. The three branches are clonal-pool examples within one target workflow. The extraction ends at the prepared library; no sequencing or long-read reconstruction operation is drawn.

method_scopes.rationale: The card title and the figure title both identify Moleculo alone. All operations belong to this single product-preparation depiction. Generate clonal pools is a branching operation, followed by branch-specific amplification, tagmentation and index addition; the three branches are not named alternative assays. This scope describes this schematic only, without generalizing its preparation to every implementation called Moleculo. No publications or publication citations are supplied, and no primary-paper association is required for this diagram.

evidence.locator: Supplied catalogue title and description: Moleculo
Whole panel: Moleculo heading and complete branched library-preparation route

unknowns.question: Does an Index 1/Index 2 combination uniquely identify each originating clonal pool, and what long-fragment provenance does that pool encode? The diagram labels indices and clonal pools but gives no index assignment, pool occupancy or reconstruction rule. A source explicitly linking indices to these pools would be needed to assert recoverable long-fragment linkage; this does not prevent extracting the depicted library preparation.

checks.rationale: Complete review of all 17 states, 13 operations and 31 flows supports the declared schematic-level architecture. The genomic DNA carrier is retained through end repair, ligation and branch-specific amplification, becomes short tagged DNA during tagmentation, receives index/P5/P7 elements, and is pooled. The branching operation is a genuine split; amplification, tagmentation and index addition remain independent local instances; the final multi-input operation is the explicitly labeled pooling. No drawn branch or transformation is omitted: each tagmentation description retains the long tagged intermediate and its arrow to the short fragment without inventing an extra reaction. Inputs, outputs, outgoing flows and Moleculo applicability agree throughout. The inferred pre-amplification boundaries are disclosed. No paper is supplied or required, no correction is claimed, and the unsupported index-to-pool assignment is explicitly withheld. The candidate digest matches the supplied canonical JSON digest.
